perspective:
**Angela Hwang’s available information:**

- She is Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate. Kevin Flores is her close friend since high school; they often confide in each other. She knows Kevin is a construction worker.
- At their coffee meeting, she invited Kevin and told him she was worried because he seemed unhappy with his job. Kevin told her he was “alright, just the usual grind”; he is not happy, feels stuck and unfulfilled, and is just going through the motions. He said he has thought about changing jobs/career but doesn’t know where to start and feels overwhelmed. She offered to figure it out together and look into options.
- She found job openings and a career counseling service and told Kevin. He thanked her. He told her he’s interested in something more creative, maybe design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources and said she thought he’d be great.
- Believing Kevin was hesitant, she arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. He said he wasn’t sure he was ready but agreed to give it a shot. She told him she believes in him and would support him.
- She checked in about the coach. Kevin told her the coach was helpful, he started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. She said she was proud and offered help. He said her support meant a lot.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career, so she organized a small celebration party and told him. He thanked her and said he was grateful. She said he’d worked hard and come far. They celebrated.
- Her own feelings/beliefs across these interactions: concerned/worried, supportive/hopeful, frustrated/worried, proud/relieved, happy/satisfied. She has no access to Kevin’s unspoken thoughts or events she did not observe/hear.
